title: Exact residue restriction before coefficient identifications
statement: For a prime l and a scheme T [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-models], there exists an additive, finite-limit- and finite-colimit-preserving Restriction l (ULift Q_l) T. Its section groups, vertical and horizontal maps and morphisms are the original ones, and z acts at level n by its residue in Z/l^(n+1). There are no Chern data, coefficient/root identifications or completed projection cones in this assertion.

source.place: paragraph (1), ordinary scalar restrictions before right derivation

proof.text: Compose the constant p-adic residue map with coefficientMap at each positive level. The completion cone and coefficientMap_transition prove compatibility with adjacent reductions. Uncurry this cone and compose with constant sections, obtaining a ring-presheaf map from constant discrete Z_l to the actual sequence ring. Restrict each module presheaf along this map and take its vertical slices, with the unchanged horizontal maps. Every underlying section, restriction, transition and morphism is definitionally the original additive one. Naturality of ring sheafification and the natural-number representative of a ZMod element identify the scalar action with the specified residue action.

The restricted slices are sheaves because their underlying additive sheaves are direct vertical restrictions of the original additive sheaf. The functor is additive componentwise. Vertical restriction is continuous and cocontinuous for the sequence topology; hence on additive sheaves it preserves finite limits and colimits. The module-to-additive-sheaf forgetful functor is exact as well. After evaluation at any level and forgetting constant scalars, the constructed functor is definitionally this exact composite. Constant scalar forgetting preserves and reflects finite limits and finite colimits. Reflect exactness through that functor and then use levelwise detection of finite limits and colimits in a functor category. A generic private conversion of constant-presheaf modules to module-valued functors keeps kernel checking from unfolding the coefficient construction.
